briefs.title: Home gym moving-quote preparation checklist
briefs.gapRationale: The specialty pillar lists exercise equipment, but the item/model/access and specialist-task handoff is absent.
briefs.readerDecision: Identify each exercise machine and the preparation/reassembly work needing a provider or specialist.
briefs.uniquePracticalArtifact: A model-specific equipment and service schedule.
outline: Record equipment brand, exact model and the owner manual
Photograph the equipment and measure its actual access route
Ask who provides any required specialist preparation and reassembly
Compare transport and specialist work as separate written responsibilities
briefs.claimBoundary: This is a quote-preparation checklist, not assembly or lifting instructions. Horizon is a limited manufacturer example. Identify each actual model and obtain its own manual; no DIY folding, lifting, cable, disassembly or electrical advice and no universal mover reassembly promise.
briefs.ctaContext: Invite the reader to describe this exact household shipment in the existing quote survey; never promise price, coverage, contact timing or a named provider.

briefs.title: Antique furniture moving-survey checklist
briefs.gapRationale: Framed artwork and general furniture preparation do not cover identifying delicate furniture surfaces, existing repairs and specialist packing decisions.
briefs.readerDecision: Give a provider a documented condition and access description while separating conservation from ordinary moving work.
briefs.uniquePracticalArtifact: An object-level condition, prior-repair and specialist-packing record.
outline: Document object identity, dimensions and current condition privately
Record loose joints, components, past repairs and sensitive finishes
Ask whether a conservator or specialist should advise before transport
Agree who supplies packing, handling and unpacking for the actual object
briefs.claimBoundary: Use the conservation source only for condition checks and the distinction between conservation and ordinary transport. No restoration, solvent, humidity target, universal wrapping or lifting instruction, assumed value, appraisal, or fabricated conservator credential.

claims.text: For interstate household-goods moves, 49 CFR 375.401 requires a written estimate covering transportation and related services.
49 CFR 375.401 permits estimate amendments before loading by mutual agreement; the section does not permit amending an estimate after loading.
FMCSA recommends obtaining several estimates and comparing the services provided, not only the quoted total.
FMCSA recommends establishing pickup and delivery arrangements and how to contact the provider before, during and after the move.
FMCSA advises reviewing completed shipment documents and not signing blank documents.
FMCSA recommends supervising loading and unloading, or asking a known person to act on the customer behalf when unavailable. This does not establish legal signing authority.
FTC recommends written estimates describing the property being moved and comparing the estimates.
FTC warns against demands for cash or a large deposit before a move. Its guidance does not set a universal legal deposit limit or refund deadline.
Boston publishes its own process for reserving moving-truck parking. This is a Boston example, not a nationwide rule.

Brookdale advises coordinating move-in with the specific community and checking what the new home includes and what belongings may be brought. This describes Brookdale guidance, not every senior-living community.
UCLA Housing says undergraduate contract dates and move-in and move-out periods vary by assigned housing location. This is a UCLA example, not a rule for other schools.

Horizon Fitness distinguishes folding and non-folding treadmills and different wheel arrangements in its moving guidance, and refers readers to the owner manual for handrail assembly. This does not establish a moving method for other brands or machines.

Olhausen Gamerooms describes breakdown, transport, reinstallation and slate crating among its own pool-table relocation arrangements. This is one provider example, not a service inclusion or warranty promise from other movers.
The Canadian Conservation Institute recommends checking wooden furniture for damage or loose joints before moving it and referring extensive repair or cleaning to a conservator.
